Guarantee

Every Interaction Human-Defined & Human-Reviewed

Genie only acts when a message matches a pattern a person already defined. If nothing matches, it does not act. You start from our policy, customize it in onboarding, and keep fine-tuning it so the behavior stays yours.

  1. 01

    Connect

    Connect your PMS or channel manager and the operational systems around it. Genie sits above the stack you already pay for.

  2. 02

    Adopt the policy

    Every company starts from our standard policy, written by people across hundreds of hospitality patterns. During onboarding, and anytime after, you rewrite the branches so Genie behaves the way your company would.

  3. 03

    Genie acts only on a match

    Genie detects the patterns you already defined. If a message matches one, it follows that policy. If it matches none, Genie does not act. No match, no abrakadabra.

Observe → Copilot → Autopilot

Enterprise teams don’t have to flip the whole company to autonomous on day one. Set the mode at the company, a department, a workflow, or a single policy.

Policy · Autopilot

Genie executes inside the policies you configured. Exceptions still come to a human.

Example: refunds under $100 execute. Refunds over $100 stay on Copilot.

Financial tracker

Every dollar, bank-checked.

Expected reservation revenue is matched to bank transactions, through a connection such as Plaid, and to card payouts such as Stripe. If a card payment is later disputed, it is flagged so the revenue is not quietly lost. Your accounting system stays your accounting system.

Case study · Superhost Management

A Case Study on an Overwhelmed Operator

120 listings in Vancouver and Los Angeles.

  1. 35% → 85%+

    Response completion

    In 35 days

  2. 4.55 → 4.83

    Average rating

    In the first 100 days

  3. 87%

The operation

Superhost Management runs stays on both sides of the border. Guest messages, turnover tasks, and the money on each reservation were already split across the tools the team paid for. Genie sat on that stack and acted only where a person had already defined the pattern.

What moved

Replies that used to stall started closing. Suggested tasks were finished instead of chased. The scoreboard they watched was the average rating, and that number rose in the first hundred days.
